method: The page implements the Wood Handbook's linear shrinkage relation for wood below the fiber saturation point. Shrinkage at moisture content x is Sx = S0 x (1 - x / 30), a percentage of the green dimension, where S0 is the species' total shrinkage from green to oven-dry from Table 4-3 and 30% MC is the fiber saturation point the handbook says to assume when it is not measured. Because the width the user measures is the width at the current moisture content, that width is first scaled back to the green dimension, green = width / (1 - S(mcNow) / 100), and then forward to the later reading, later = green x (1 - S(mcLater) / 100); the movement is later - width. Tangential shrinkage is used for flat-sawn widths and radial shrinkage for quarter-sawn ones, as the handbook specifies, and the page also reports what quarter-sawn stock would move for the same board. The 27 species presets are Table 4-3 values transcribed as printed (for example northern red oak 4.0% radial and 8.6% tangential, white oak 5.6% and 10.5%, eastern white pine 2.1% and 6.1%); they are species averages, and the handbook puts the coefficient of variation at about 15% for a single piece, with reaction wood, juvenile wood and mixed ring angles moving more than the average suggests. Widths are entered in inches or millimetres (1 in = 25.4 mm) and the result is reported in the unit used, with the movement per 1% of moisture change. Moisture readings are limited to 0-30%, because above fiber saturation the free water in the cell cavities changes weight but not size: a reading above 30% is rejected with an explanation rather than silently clamped. Widths are limited to 1-12,700 mm (0.04-500 in). Only the cross-grain width moves; longitudinal shrinkage is 0.1-0.2% and is ignored. The result is an allowance for grooves, slots, breadboard ends and frame and panel clearances, not a substitute for measuring the board in the shop.

sources.title: Glass, S.V. and Zelinka, S.L., USDA Forest Service Forest Products Laboratory: Wood Handbook, Chapter 4 'Moisture Relations and Physical Properties of Wood' (FPL-GTR-282, 2021) — shrinkage at moisture content x is Sx = S0 (1 - x/MCfs) (Eq. 4-9) with 30% MC assumed for the fiber saturation point, tangential S0 for flat-sawn widths and radial S0 for quarter-sawn, and Table 4-3 green-to-ovendry shrinkage percentages by species
